dialogue.speaker: Orin
dialogue.text: The houses are empty, but the wells are clean. We can stop running here.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: My orders say you are dangerous.

dialogue.speaker: Orin
dialogue.text: Then watch what we do. We will hold the houses, not march on yours.

dialogue.speaker: Dain
dialogue.text: You put your archers between my patrol and those villagers. My orders did not mention that.

dialogue.speaker: Orin
dialogue.text: The man who wrote your orders used to write mine.

dialogue.speaker: Dain
dialogue.text: Then I know which road we take next.

dialogue.speaker: Orin
dialogue.text: We have little use for the herbs. The people next door do. They insist on paying us. I think that is what neighbors do.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Vale
dialogue.text: The factor pays us to keep this channel clear for salvage. Bring your accusation to the council; you will not cross my posts.

dialogue.speaker: Factor Senn
dialogue.text: That ledger is company property. Vale, clear the landing.

dialogue.speaker: Edda
dialogue.text: I can bring them out along the keel. Hold this landing until the sixth bell; nobody touches the quarry gate before then.

dialogue.speaker: Edda
dialogue.text: I need three ferry crossings to bring everyone out along the keel. Hold the landing. The last boat leaves with the sixth bell's high tide, or later if we are delayed; nobody touches the quarry gate before then.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: A debt cannot give you ownership of a person. We take the books after we get everyone out.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: Three groves marked for cutting. The soldiers say we killed their woodcutters.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Then take the groves back. Leave their fort alone; we need the cutting stopped, not another graveyard.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: You want us gone? Prove those roots hide something other than your own crimes.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: All three groves are ours again. The cutters have put down their axes.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: After what has happened here, I will not call us friends. But I will hear what you know about the missing woodcutters.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Come to the central grove under a truce. Lark can wake the roots and show us what they remember.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: Dain is gone. We can still stop the cutting and find out what happened to the woodcutters.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The three groves are ours, but Dain will never see what lies beneath them.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: His death will not bring back the woodcutters. Tamsin asked to hear the roots; let her come under a truce.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: Tools, not trophies. Leave them where their owners will find them. There are six coins tucked in the handle; we can use those for the vigil.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: They call the trees an obstacle. They have marked three groves for cutting.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Then we stand where their marks are. No chase into their fort. We need our roots back, not their bones.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The wolves know the narrow paths. Their hunters know where to point a spear. Let the boars go first when the woods run out.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: We came for timber. Something in the old grove has been killing our woodcutters. Was that you?

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: No. Come back at dusk, with empty hands, and I will show you what wakes beneath the stones.

dialogue.speaker: Dain
dialogue.text: The households are meeting in the northern village. I will tell them why my patrol fought the wrong people.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The branch carries the woodcutters’ memory. The Rootbinder would rather burn it than let their families listen.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Take the bridge fort so the villagers can cross safely. Lark can use whichever path gets her to the meeting alive.

dialogue.speaker: Tamsin
dialogue.text: Dain sent for me. Some of those woodcutters were my neighbors. I will help clear your road; their families need the truth, not another duel with their master.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The branch has flowered. The households have heard what happened beneath the grove.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: And the fort is ours. No one must ask the overseer’s leave to cross this river again.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: We will keep the road open together. The Rootbinder can hide from us, but he cannot hide the truth now.

dialogue.speaker: Tamsin
dialogue.text: The households are meeting in the northern village. I saw the grove’s memory; I will stand beside you when they hear it.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The households have heard the woodcutters. Dain is among the names we must remember, too.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: The fort is ours and the meeting has chosen an open road. That is a promise we can still keep.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: Then let the first travelers cross. We have enough graves; we need neighbors.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: Someone left these for a traveler who never came. Today, someone will.

dialogue.speaker: Dain
dialogue.text: Lark carries a living branch. When it flowers, no one can pretend the grove was only lumber.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: It will flower. But I would rather not test that while a skeleton is shooting at me.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Secure the bridge. The witness comes first. Dain, your spears and our boars hold the open road together.

dialogue.speaker: Tamsin
dialogue.text: The dead hardly feel arrows, but stone sparks crack bone. Let the shields hold them while I work. Lark can rest in the groves beyond the ford.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: It flowered.

dialogue.speaker: Dain
dialogue.text: Then I will say what I saw. And I will keep saying it until they hear.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Leave the bridge open. That is what a pact is for.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: I came without my patrol. The truce holds while I watch from the treeline.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: Bring me to the central grove. I need three quiet nights with the roots; if I must leave, the memory slips away.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Then we stand around you. The overseer would not send soldiers to silence an empty story.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The roots have spoken. The Rootbinder killed the woodcutters and raised their bodies to serve the overseer.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: I saw his seal on the dead. We fought you on a lie. The villages must hear what happened, even if it costs me my command.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: I will bring their memory and this living branch. Let the households hear the dead and judge the living.

dialogue.speaker: Tamsin
dialogue.text: I will watch from the treeline. Dain is gone, but the families still deserve to know who killed their woodcutters.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Then we stand around you. Let the roots answer where swords could not.

dialogue.speaker: Tamsin
dialogue.text: I saw his seal on the dead. I will take you to the village meeting. Dain’s death cannot excuse what his employer has done.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The owls found a forgotten patrol cache. Better six coins for a living grove than for another axe.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: The grove needs one night to recover. We hold it until dawn.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The overseer has sent patrols along both roads. One on the third turn, another on the fifth. The wooden forts are theirs only while they stand in them.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: I saw the thing under the stones. It wore a dead man’s face and my lord’s seal.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Then take our witness to your people. A forest and a village can share a road.
